_readme: Every building in the game. Edit the numbers here, save, restart - no rebuild.
ID IS PERMANENT. Save files store what you own as an array keyed by these ids,
so changing an id or reusing a retired one silently loads the wrong buildings
into the wrong slots on every existing save. Reordering entries in this file is
safe; renumbering them is not. New buildings take the next unused id.
Money is in thousands: cashCost 30 is $30,000.
constructionMaterials is in units of material worth $18,000 each at world prices - a
House takes ten, so a unit is a tenth of a house's structure. cashCost is everything
else: the work, the equipment, the fit-out. A building COSTS cashCost + 18 x materials.
Water is in units of 10,000 gallons/month.
land is the lot footprint in square feet; a city block is 100,000.
roadLoad is the traffic a building puts on the road network each month.
For INFRASTRUCTURE, capacity is the road capacity the building provides;
and transitCapacity is commuter journeys a month a bus, tram or metro can carry.
For RAIL, railCapacity is tonnes a month the network can move across the city
boundary. Rail is a SECTOR ("sector": "Rail"), so the investor builds it, not the city.
the city starts with 400 of it for free. Traffic flows freely up to 90% of
capacity and then degrades, so headroom is what matters, not the raw total.
WHO OWNS IT, AND WHAT IT MAKES. 'sector' is the owning business by its saved name -
Retail, Real Estate, Industry, Construction, Heavy Industry, Mining, Materials - and
a building with no sector is the city's (roads, plants, schools, clinics) or the
bank's. 'makes' and 'uses' are units of a GOOD a month per building at nameplate:
"makes": { "STEEL": 1200 }, "uses": { "SCRAP": 1320 }
Goods are FOOD (a person-month of food), IRON (tonnes of ore), SCRAP (tonnes, 0.7.120),
STEEL (tonnes), MATERIALS (a unit of building material), GROCERIES
(food on a shelf, sold to households), HOUSING (homes), BUILDING_WORK (points).
Prices are on the goods, not here: the world charges and pays a fixed price for
each, and the city's markets clear between the two. 'stock' is the room a
building has for what it holds - a plant's warehouse, a shop's shelf - in units.
For a store, 'coverage' is people it can serve a month and it makes that many
GROCERIES out of that much FOOD. For a home, 'makes' HOUSING is its dwellings.
A mine also needs a DEPOSIT: buy a land parcel with iron under it. An Oil Well
needs an oil site the same way, one a well: a MINING building stands on the sites
of the resource whose good it makes.
Since 0.7.110 it says so: "site": {"resource": "IRON", "type": "HEMATITE", "sites":
1, "dig": 1} is the resource, the type of field it needs (HEMATITE or MAGNETITE for
iron, THERMAL or COKING for coal, SULPHIDE or OXIDE for copper, LIMESTONE or HARD_ROCK
for stone, or ANY), the sites it takes and the tonnes of field a unit it makes takes
out. An Offshore Platform's jacket takes none: its wells do. No site, no deposit asked.
Since 0.7.124 every iron mine stands on a type: the Iron Mine and the Large Open-Pit
Mine on HEMATITE, the Magnetite Mine & Concentrator and the Large Magnetite Complex on
MAGNETITE, digging 3 t of rock for a tonne of concentrate; and a works of 20 sites
needs 20 free sites of ONE field of its type (LandManager.fits()), its iron the
tonnes of its type still in the ground. Since 0.7.126 coal's do: the Surface Coal
Mine and the Large Surface Mine (four sites of one field) on THERMAL, digging 1/.95 t
of seam a tonne; the Underground Coal Mine on COKING at 1/.80, its coal RAW.
A well stands only on a dry site (a field whose centre is on land), lifts 10%
less each year and is retired under ten barrels a day, after 263 months.
CRUDE is tonnes of crude oil, lifted by the wells and refined. A refinery 'uses'
CRUDE and 'makes' nothing of its own: its products - petrol, diesel and the rest,
in litres - are the cuts of the crude it runs (sectors.Refining, THE SLATE), its
'stock' the tanks they share; the drivers draw the petrol, the railway the diesel.
A refinery's CONVERSION UNIT (a reformer, a cracking unit, a coker...) buys and
makes nothing of its own either: "refinery": {"unit": "REFORMER", "feed": 1161495}
says its kind and the litres a month of its feed stream it takes from the crude
units' run (sectors.RefineryFlow): REFORMER, CRACKER, HYDROCRACKER, ALKYLATION,
COKER, LUBE or ASPHALT.
A FILLING STATION ("pump": 350000) is the grocers' forecourt: it buys and makes
nothing on a market of its own. Retail draws the drivers' petrol at wholesale and
sells it at the pump (sectors.Retail, THE FORECOURTS); 'pump' is the litres a month
a station sells at its typical throughput. LUBRICANTS in a factory's 'uses' are
litres of oil on its line: 8 a vehicle built, 10 a tonne of machinery, 2 a tonne of
fabricated steel (runs/spec-oil.md 2.5).
A TANK FARM is the refiners' storage: its 'stock' is litres of tank room (500,000
m3). With one standing the refiners keep a month of their crude units' crude on
hand in it and their products share the rest (sectors.Refining, THE TANK FARM). A
STRATEGIC RESERVE is the same tanks owned by the city, holding crude oil only: the
city fills it and releases it in the month's crude market (StrategicReserve).
A PORTS building is one of the city's sea terminals: "port": {"cargo": "LIQUID",
"tonnes": 3250000} is the kind of cargo its berth handles - LIQUID, DRY_BULK,
CONTAINER or GENERAL - and the tonnes a year. It needs the city to own some sea, and
the kind's goods go by sea in the share its berths cover (Ports).
THE OIL AT SEA: "offshore": {"kind": "PLATFORM", "slots": 12} is an Offshore
Platform's jacket, standing on a shallow sea field the city owns (150 m deep at most)
with slots for 12 wells, at most one a sea site of its field; {"kind": "WELL"} is a
Platform Well in one of them, lifting its crude as a land well does, held three
years then 8.5% less a year; {"kind": "PIPELINE", "onshore": 3000} is a
kilometre of Crude Pipeline (its cash a kilometre at sea, "onshore" one on land),
which takes a field's crude ashore in place of the shuttle tankers. They stand at
sea and take none of the city's dry ground (sectors.Oil).
production1 / production2 survive only for the utilities: watts for ELECTRICITY,
water units for WATER.
A WATER building draws fresh water unless it says "source": "SEA". Fresh water is
held to what the lakes and river the city owns yield (121,600 units a month a km2);
a SEA building is not held to it, and needs the city to own some sea.
A ROAD's "repairs" is its own repairs a year, a share of what it cost to put up
(0.7.103; every other building is repaired at 1% a year), from the Canadian
Infrastructure Report Card 2016's target reinvestment rates a year of replacement
value (Key Messages, Figure 4; informative only, the report says): roads and
sidewalks 2.0-3.0%, the Gravel Road at the top (3%, its surface renewed oftener) and the
Paved Road at the bottom (2%); bridges 1-1.5%, the Elevated Highway at the middle
(1.25%). See BuildingsTemplate, A ROAD'S OWN REPAIRS.
A WORKS may make power itself (0.7.112): "gen" is the kW it makes. It buys from the
grid only what it draws past that, and sells the grid what it makes past its draw, at
the tariff. "consumables" is what a works buys abroad that is not a good - refractories,
reagents, spares - in thousands of the WORLD's money a month at nameplate, paid at the
exchange factor at the share of nameplate it runs. Since 0.7.123 the Coke Ovens (8,000),
the Blast Furnace (60,000) and the Oxygen Steel Shop (25,000) make power; since 0.7.120
the Iron Mine (explosives and wear parts) and the arc furnaces (electrodes), and since
0.7.123 every works of Iron & Steel, and since 0.7.124 every mine, buy consumables: the
study's running cost less wages, the power it buys, water and diesel.
A SCRAP YARD takes the city's OLD STEEL - its scrapped cars, its demolitions, its
fabricators' offcuts, its worn-out wagon sets, which arise each month and are not a
good: "oldMetal": {"STEEL": 10500} is the tonnes a month it takes at nameplate,
paying the sellers 70% of scrap's export price (0.7.123; see OldMetal). What no yard
takes goes to landfill.
"since" is the year a building first existed (0.7.123), 1900 - the start year - for one
that stood before it; read by nothing yet, for research (absent: not yet dated).
A COAL PREPARATION PLANT ("wash": 500000, 0.7.126) washes the raw coal Coal Mining's
mines on coking fields dig, tonnes a month at nameplate, into coking coal (55%) and
thermal coal (20%), the rest to spoil; raw coal no plant washes sells as thermal coal,
tonne for tonne. Raw coal is not a good: the plant buys and makes none of its own, and
the sector's flow says what comes of it (sectors.CoalMining).
For HEALTHCARE, 'care' says what the building treats and 'capacity' is how
many of those people it has room for: CHILDCARE counts babies and children,
SENIOR counts seniors, GENERAL counts everyone and is what decides how much
of the workforce is off sick. BURIAL and CREMATION serve the dead instead, so
their capacity is measured against deaths, not against a share of the living.
A healthcare building with no 'care' line treats nobody.
For SAFETY, 'safety' says what the building does: POLICE, whose 'capacity' is
sworn officers (full coverage is 360 per 100,000 people, twice Canada's level),
or PRISON, whose 'capacity' is cells, each holding one prisoner for a six-month
sentence. Both are cut by how much of the staff the city can fill.
Any field you leave out defaults to 0, so a House needs no 'coverage' line.
jobs keys are JobType names: NO_DIPLOMA, DIPLOMA, COLLEGE_HEALTH,
COLLEGE_BUSINESS, COLLEGE_ENGINEERING, UNIV_DOCTOR, UNIV_LAW, UNIV_FINANCE,
UNIV_SCIENCE, UNIV_HIGHTECH_ENG, UNIV_POLICY.
If this file is missing or malformed the game falls back to its built-in
buildings and prints why, so a typo here can never stop it starting.
